subject: Private endpoint egress & allowlist checklist - Nimbus POC
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.k@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Private endpoint egress/allowlist checklist for Nimbus POC

Hi Monica / Marissa,

Thanks for partnering with us on the POC. To get our staging environment talking to your private endpoints, security needs a concise allowlist + firewall policy that we can hand to our networking team. Can you provide a checklist that covers at least:

- Required outbound destinations (hostnames and, where unavoidable, IP ranges) for Redwood control plane and model fetch.
- Ports/protocols we need to open (eg. 443, 123 for NTP if required).
- Guidance on DNS and whether SNI-based allowlisting is sufficient or we need static IP entries / NAT with source-IP allowlist.
- Any client certs / mTLS expectations for private endpoints.
- Expected egress for telemetry, metrics and usage-reporting endpoints.
- Notes on long-lived connections (WebSocket/streaming) and idle timeout recommendations.

I've attached our POC requirements and a network snapshot. If you have a short template we can use, that would speed approvals.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Khan
Infrastructure Lead, Nimbus Analytics
samir.k@nimbus-analytics.com
Attachment: nimbus_poc_requirements.xlsx (Excel)
Attachment: network-snapshot.pdf (PDF)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood-inference.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Private endpoint egress/allowlist checklist for Nimbus POC

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list. Below is a pragmatic checklist and rationale to hand to your networking team. I’ve kept hostnames first (preferred) and IP ranges second (only for strict NAT environments).

1) Control plane (required outbound HTTPS):
   - Hostnames: api.redwood-inference.com, control.redwood-inference.com
   - Ports: 443 (HTTPS) only
   - IP ranges (if you cannot allow by hostname/SNI): 54.210.33.0/24, 3.120.44.0/24 (sample ranges — please confirm with us before adding to a permanent ACL)

2) Model and artifact fetch (optional during POC if you host models remotely):
   - Hostnames: storage.redwood-inference.com, s3.amazonaws.com (if using S3-backed model bundles)
   - Ports: 443
   - Note: We recommend allowing these hostnames only for the nodes that will fetch large model artifacts. Use a temporary NAT IP entry or pre-stage models in your internal artifact store to avoid large egress during demos.

3) Telemetry / Metrics / Usage reporting:
   - Hostnames: telemetry.redwood-inference.com, metrics.redwood-inference.com
   - Ports: 443
   - Pattern: Batched HTTPS POSTs. If your egress policy blocks unknown destinations, whitelist these hostnames.

4) DNS and SNI guidance:
   - Preferred: allow hostname/SNI-based egress at the HTTP layer and use your internal resolver — this reduces brittle IP ACLs.
   - Fallback: If your org requires source-IP allowlist, route outbound through a dedicated NAT gateway with static IP(s) and share those IPs with us.

5) mTLS / client auth:
   - Redwood control plane supports TLS with server certs. For Private deployments we offer optional mTLS for control-plane webhook/console callbacks — enable if your security policy requires client cert validation.
   - If you enable mTLS, we will provide CA and client cert instructions.

6) Long-lived streaming sockets:
   - We use HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming and HTTP/2 for streaming responses. Expect idle keepalive and occasional re-connects. Recommend idle timeouts >= 120s for streaming routes.

7) NTP / time sync and CRL/OCSP:
   - Time sync: Allow outbound NTP (UDP/123) or ensure local NTP resolver.
   - CRL/OCSP: TLS revocation checks may reach certificate authorities — allow egress to common OCSP responders if you enforce strict revocation checks on the network edge.

8) Egress for package updates (optional):
   - If your on-prem nodes need apt/yum access, either pre-seed packages or allow access to your internal update proxies. We do not require package manager access to function but models may need system libs if you build from source.

Mutual action plan (suggested):
- Step 1: Nimbus infra whitelists hostnames above in staging and routes through a static NAT IP (if required).
- Step 2: Run the quick connectivity test (redwood-connectivity-test.sh) from one staging node and paste results. (I attached the script to this thread.)
- Step 3: If streaming routes fail, increase idle timeout and confirm SNI passthrough on TLS inspection device.

I attached the connectivity test script and a lightweight one-page checklist PDF. Happy to walk your networking team through the steps — can we schedule a 30m call? I’m available Thu/Fri PST.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood-inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0122
Attachment: redwood-connectivity-test.sh (executable script)

From: Samir Khan <samir.k@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Private endpoint egress/allowlist checklist for Nimbus POC

Monica — this is great, thanks. A couple quick clarifications from our security team:

- We run a TLS inspection appliance that terminates TLS and re-encrypts (SNI is visible, but downstream IPs differ). Is SNI-based allowlisting sufficient in that case or do you require raw destination IPs?
- For telemetry endpoints, can we batch to an internal aggregator instead of allowing outbound telemetry.redwood-inference.com? We prefer to proxy telemetry through our internal gateway and only allow the NAT IP.
- For mTLS: are client certs per-customer or per-node? The network team wants to understand rotation cadence and automation options.

Also attached: a short export of our current NAT IPs and firewall policy so you can see how we normally map hostnames to ACLs.

If convenient, we’d take the 30m call on Friday at 09:00 PST. 

—Samir
Attachment: nimbus-nat-ips.csv (CSV)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood-inference.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Private endpoint egress/allowlist checklist for Nimbus POC

Samir — good questions. Short answers below, and then proposed ops decisions.

- TLS inspection / SNI: SNI-based allowlisting is usually sufficient for the control plane and telemetry because we authenticate at the HTTP layer (TLS server certs) and validate Host/SNI. If your TLS inspection rewrites host headers or terminates and replaces certs such that original SNI/Host is not preserved upstream, you'll need to use NAT source-IP allowlists for the outbound gateway.

- Telemetry via internal aggregator: perfectly fine — proxying telemetry through your internal gateway and allowing a single NAT egress IP is an OK pattern for POC. Just ensure the aggregator forwards the original Host header or uses a mapping we agree on.

- mTLS: client certs are issued per-customer for control-plane callbacks (not per-node). Certificate rotation is typically quarterly by default, and we can support automated renewal via your internal cert management tooling (ACME or internal CA).

Operations decisions to minimize friction:
- Use hostname/SNI allowlist for staging nodes.
- If you must use TLS inspection that breaks SNI, route Redwood-bound traffic through a dedicated NAT IP and share that IP with us for a temporary ACL.
- Proxy telemetry internally for the POC; we’ll accept the NAT IP for telemetry endpoints.
- For mTLS, we’ll provide a single client cert per Nimbus account + rotation guidance.

Next steps:
- I confirmed Friday 09:00 PST for a 30m connectivity + firewall walkthrough. Please invite your network engineer and any SREs.
- Run the redwood-connectivity-test.sh from one staging node and paste the output before the call.

Thanks — look forward to the call.

Monica
